Subject: Exit channels & outbound demarcation for private connectors

Brian —

Thanks again for taking the call today. As we scope the Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for Acme, we want to pin down the outbound/egress requirements so we can produce an ops-safe runbook and a short PoC matrix. A few items we need clarified from your side: 

- Do all outbound flows from your private connectors exit through a central NAT gateway or are there per-subnet egress breakouts?
- Are you comfortable with a small set of static egress IP ranges for Redwood to allowlist, or do you require proxy termination (mTLS) on your side?
- Will DNS be resolved at the customer VPC (split-horizon) or via your central resolver? Any CNAME rewriting/HTTP SNI concerns?
- What logging/audit expectations do you have for the control plane connections (flow logs, netflow, TLS fingerprints)?

Attached: outbound-matrix.xlsx (stub) — a proposed matrix for short-term and long-term options.

We want to propose an "exit-channel" concept: classify outbound flows by purpose (control plane, model fetch/cache, telemetry) and map each to a specific egress demarcation (static IPs, proxy, regional NAT). That helps minimize blast radius and satisfies allowlisting requirements.

Can you confirm the NAT ranges and whether a forward proxy is in scope?

Thanks,

Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Brian Turner <brian.turner@acmehealth.com>

Date: 2026-11-01T13:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Exit channels & outbound demarcation for private connectors

Marcus —

Appreciate the detail. Quick summary from netops: 

- All egress exits through a central NAT/egress gateway in each region. We do have per-VPC route tables but we push outbound through the gateway for audit and DLP.
- We prefer static IP allowlisting for vendor integrations. We can accommodate up to three /28 blocks per vendor (subject to change with advance notice).
- For high-trust partners we run an internal forward proxy that can accept client certs (mutual TLS). If you can support mTLS to our proxy that’s ideal for control plane and telemetry.
- DNS: split-horizon. Internal names resolve to private IPs; public names go out via our resolvers which apply CNAME rewriting for certain domains. This can impact SNI-based routing and certificate pinning if endpoints do not expect rewritten names.
- Logs: we require flow logs + proxy access logs for all control-plane egress. Retention 1 year.

We can share the NAT ranges once we confirm the vendor contract terms. Also, we need an operational runbook showing fallbacks: e.g., if proxy is unreachable, do you retry to IPs or fail closed?

-Brian
Brian Turner
Head of Network Engineering, Acme Health

Brian —

Thanks for the clear answers. Short summary of our proposed approach for the PoC and production roll: 

1) Exit-channel mapping (PoC):
   - control-plane (auth, telemetry): TLS to Acme proxy with mTLS; allowlist a small, documented set of egress IPs as fallback.
   - model artifacts & large fetches (S3/registry): static IP allowlist from regional NAT pools; prefer caching on the customer-side where possible.
   - ephemeral inference outbound (callbacks, webhooks): map to a distinct egress set and require webhook endpoints to verify TLS and signed payloads.

2) DNS behavior: we will ensure the Redwood client respects split-horizon and uses your VPC resolver by default. For any domain with CNAME rewriting we will surface SNI mismatches in the PoC tests.

3) Logging & compliance: We will emit detailed flow metadata and proxy TLS fingerprints to your collector. Will keep 1yr retention for audit purposes.

4) Failover policy: default to fail-closed for control-plane calls; model fetch retries will attempt regional NAT fallback up to 3x before failing. We will document the retry windows.

Action items: 
- Brian: share NAT ranges and proxy cert requirements.
- Acme netops: confirm if a short-term whitelist (3 /28s) is acceptable for PoC.
- Soojin/Network: please review the short-term architecture & propose an implementation plan and runbook.

Attaching a short spec: private-connectors-egress-spec.md (stub) and linking a drive folder with the PoC timeline.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Laura / team —

Notes from a networking implementation perspective (short-term -> long-term):

Short-term (PoC, 2 weeks):
- Accept static allowlist: we will provide two regional egress IP blocks (one primary, one warm standby). Request: Acme to confirm the exact /28s.
- Transparent forward proxy option: deploy a lightweight forward proxy in the customer VPC that terminates TLS and forwards via our control plane with client certs. This reduces DNS/SNI friction but requires proxy access logs to be forwarded to Acme.
- Health checks and circuit breakers: envelope-level retries with exponential backoff; control-plane will fail-closed after 2 consecutive 5s timeouts.

Long-term (3–6 months):
- mTLS origination on the customer edge for control-plane; Redwood will support mutual TLS and certificate rotation using ACME or customer-provided CA.
- Split-horizon-aware resolver in our agent so we don't accidentally leak internal hostnames; fallback to explicit resolver IPs supplied during onboarding.
- Per-service egress tagging so Acme can map flows to audit categories (control, telemetry, artifact).

Runbook checklist we will produce: egress IP list, proxy cert format (PEM + SAN requirements), DNS resolver config, expected logs (fields & formats), SLA for failover.

Let me know if we should include a short iptables vs. proxy decision matrix for on-prem customers.

-Soojin
Principal Network Engineer
Redwood Inference
